result:
**The plan:** writing-skills was the last of 41 files that plan 43's drift sweep had marked stale against the Claude Code guide. Its Claude Code material sat in `discovery.md` alongside lint rules and runtime-neutral advice. Some claims there were wrong or unsupported: descriptions "always resident", `@` force-loading 200k+ tokens, and fork advice resting on a lapsed premise. Two register entries also waited on a rewrite. Per the owner's decisions, the plan was to distill the Claude Code facts into one file, keep the Iron Law, and review against the guide on main.

**The build:** First came a pre-registered micro-test kit: four frozen cases, prompt builders, isolated `claude -p` reps, and rules committed before any run. Next, the old layout was tested. The RED control passed 5/5, so no template rule was added. Opus failed P3a 0/5, each time giving the stale fork reason. Then came the new 64-line `references/claude-code.md`, covering frontmatter keys, Haiku `model`, a corrected fork rationale, listing overflow and compaction budgets. `discovery.md` and `SKILL.md` were trimmed to portable advice with pointers to it. New-layout reps met all bars, and P3a rose to 5/5, with stated limits. A 56-row manual review followed. The citation was restamped at `@2.1.306` across eight sections, and the register, NOTICE and history were updated.

**The project:** Claude Code facts now live in one small, guide-backed file that other runtimes skip unless they follow the pointer. The drift-sweep stale list is empty, and two older backlog items are closed. Future guide changes will re-flag the skill as intended. Several gaps are deferred, including read-before-edit testing.
